name: Dividend durability
summary: A 3%+ dividend yield, covered by free cash flow, with moderate debt and no cut in five years.
how_to_read: Four filters must all pass: a dividend yield of at least 3%, dividends at most 70% of free cash flow, net debt at most 3× EBITDA, and no cut of more than 1% in dividends per share across the last five fiscal years. Companies with fewer than five years of filings, or with negative FCF, have no value for those tests and fail them.
misses: What comes next: every test looks backwards, and a dividend that has been safe can still be cut.
REITs, where FCF and EBITDA work differently (they pay from FFO), so few appear.
Banks, insurers and capital-markets firms, where net debt / EBITDA isn't meaningful, so none appear.
